name: 1628 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws the building crossed by one X, the key's sign for a stable (the T-1840 census: '2-storey brick stable (X) on the alley'), and Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses the brick building it draws on the same ground, the atlas's stable. Carried to 1904 between the two, INFERRED; no source names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, beside 1626's stable (the two share one wall on the sheet). The sheet census (census row s20-1628-r1, trace s20fp-1628-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The kit stands as drawn, its party wall at the north end on the wall line it shares with 1626's and its open gable to the south, where the sheet marks no window. Its alley wall, 7.0 m long, has the sheet's window mark at its middle, so the kit's carriage bay is built where the mark stands (the mark is the key's sign for openings in both storeys, not for a sash). Robinson's 1886 plate draws the same pair of crossed brick stables at nearly the same sizes, so this one stood from before 1886 through 1911. No picture of it is known. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1626-1628-stables-1932/README.md.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it. Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a pink, crossed building on the alley across the rears of lots 16 and 17 in two parts, each about 7.3 m along the alley (pink-density profiles on the committed plate raster at its 0.346 m a pixel: rows 1222, 1243 and 1264.6), the north part about 11.1 m deep (columns 342-374) and the south part about 14.5 m (columns 341-383): within the plate's line widths, the two buildings the 1911 sheet draws, 1626's 7.97 by 11.87 m and 1628's 7.01 by 13.94 m. The 1911 sheet draws it again, so it stood from before 1886 through 1911 and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), as the district draft did. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

This position is pixel (2225.06, 3015.95) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2225.1) to its east wall line (2499.5) and from the wall line it shares with 1626's building (row 2947.0) to its south wall line (3084.9), each the peak of a median darkness profile: 274.4 by 138.0 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 13.935 m deep by 7.008 m along the alley.

stories.note: '2' lettered on the building: two storeys.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 8' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) on the wall line it shares with 1626's and again inside its south wall. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours it pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1626-1628-stables-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8', a stable's X, and one of the key's window marks, on the alley wall about 3.71 m from the wall line it shares with 1626's, with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there). It draws no fire-wall sign and no other mark on this building. The kit stands as drawn: its party wall at the north end, on that shared wall line, back to back with 1626's party wall (1626's kit is the mirror image); its open gable at the south end, with no opening, as the sheet marks none. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley wall's from the north end, the yard wall's from the south end, as the kit lays them). The alley wall is 7.0 m long and the mark stands at its middle, so the kit's carriage bay (2.7 m clear, its narrowest) cannot stand beside a sash at the mark with the 0.1 m the kit keeps between openings: the mark is read as the carriage bay with the loft hatch over it, centred where the mark stands (the key's mark says only that both storeys are open there, which a carriage bay and its hatch are). A man door with a loft sash over it toward the north end and a stable sash with a loft sash over it toward the south end are the kit's. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees (1616's, 1612's and 1736's deep-stable pitch) over the 13.94 m span, about 4.0 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 0.5 m from its south wall and 6.1 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's main rear wall, 15.2 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's window mark where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
